entries.def:
προθύμως 
[in LXX: 2Ch.29.34 (יָשָׁר לֵבָב), Tob.7.8, al. ;] 
eagerly, readily, with a ready mind: 1Pe.5.2.†
(AS)

προ-καλέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: 2Ma.8.11 A * ;] 
to call forth. 
Most frequently in mid., 
__(a) to challenge; hence, to provoke: Gal.5.26 
__(b) to invite (2Mac, l.with).†
(AS)

προ-κατ-αγγέλλω 
to announce beforehand: with accusative and inf., Act.3.18 before περί, Act.7.52.†
(AS)

πρό-κειμαι 
[in LXX: Exo.39.18 (36), Num.4.7 (פָּנִים), etc. ;] 
used as pass. of προτίθημι; 
__1. to be set before one, to be set forth: Heb.6.18; 12.1-2, Jude.7. 
__2. to present oneself, be present: 2Co.8.12 (see Mey., in l).†
(AS)

προ-κηρύσσω 
__1. to proclaim by herald. 
__2. Of one who acts as a herald, to proclaim: Act.13.24.†
(AS)

προ-κοπή, -ῆς, ἡ
(προκόπτω), [in LXX: Sir.51.17, 2Ma.8.8 * ;] 
progress (prop., on a journey, then generally): Php.1.12, 25, 1Ti.4.15 (condemned by Atticists, see Rutherford, NPhr., 158).†
(AS)

προ-κόπτω 
[in Sm.: Psa.45.5 * ;] 
to cut forward a way, for­ward, advance, in cl. trans. with neut. adj., as οὐδὲν π., τὰ πολλὰ π. In late writers (Polyb., al.), wholly intrans., to advance, progress: of time, Rom.13.12. Metaphorical, Luk.2.52, Gal.1.14, 2Ti.2.16; 3.9; 3.13.†
(AS)

πρό-κριμα, -τος, τό
(cl. προκρίνειν, 1. to prefer. 2. to judge beforehand), 
pre-judging, prejudice: 1Ti.5.21 (see Cremer, 378).†
(AS)
